notes.meaning: Paul opens his letter by calling himself a servant, or bond-slave, of Jesus Christ. He explains that he did not choose this job on his own, but was called by God to be an apostle, a special messenger sent with divine authority. God set him apart for the specific purpose of telling people the good news of salvation. Believers can take comfort knowing that God gives each of His servants a clear calling.

Paul points out that the good news of Jesus was not an invention or an afterthought. God had promised this message centuries earlier through the Old Testament prophets in the Holy Scriptures. This shows that the Christian message fulfills the ancient plan God laid out long ago.

The core of the gospel message is God's Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. In His earthly human life, Jesus was born into the family line of King David as the prophets had foretold. This fulfilled God's ancient promise that the Messiah would come from David's royal lineage.

While Jesus was truly human, His bodily resurrection from the dead openly proved that He is the powerful Son of God. His resurrection showed His holy divine nature to the whole world beyond any doubt. Death could not hold Him because He is the Lord of life.

differ.view: Christ was appointed or inaugurated as the Son of God in power at His resurrection regarding His office in salvation history, rather than gaining divinity He did not previously possess.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Verses 3 and 4 may preserve an early Christian confession or creed that existed before Paul wrote this letter.

notes.meaning: Through Christ, Paul received both God's special favor and the calling of an apostle. His mission was to bring people from all non-Jewish nations to the obedience that flows from true faith. True faith in Jesus always leads to a life that seeks to obey Him and honor His name.

Paul reminds the Roman believers that they belong to the very group God has called. They share the same standing in Christ as believers from any other nation. Hearing God's voice in the gospel means being welcomed into His family.

Paul sends his greeting to all the believers in Rome, describing them as deeply loved by God and called to be saints, which means people set apart for holy living. He blesses them with grace, which is God's undeserved kindness, and peace, which is wholeness and reconciliation with God. These gifts flow directly from both God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul begins with praise, thanking God through Jesus Christ for the whole church in Rome. People all across the Roman empire were talking about their strong faith. It brings great joy when Christians hear good reports about the faith of others.

Paul calls God as his witness that he prays for the Roman church faithfully and from his whole heart. He regularly asks God to open a way for him to visit Rome at last, if it is God's will. Faithful believers put their travel plans and desires into God's hands.

Paul longs to visit the Romans so he can share spiritual blessings with them through his teaching and help them stand firm. At the same time, he explains that their meeting will be a mutual encouragement, where both his faith and theirs will strengthen one another. Even experienced leaders need the fresh encouragement of fellow believers.

Paul explains that he had often planned to visit Rome, but other urgent ministry needs had kept him away until now. He wanted to see spiritual fruit among them, meaning people coming to faith and growing in maturity, just as he had seen in other places. God sometimes changes our travel plans so other important work can be finished first.

Paul feels a heavy obligation to preach the good news to everyone, whether they are cultured Greeks, outside nations, educated thinkers, or simple folk. Because of this calling, he is fully ready to preach the gospel in Rome, the empire's greatest city. The message of Jesus is meant for every kind of person in the world.

Paul is not ashamed of the gospel, even though worldly thinkers treated it as foolishness and weakness. The message of the cross carries God's mighty power to deliver everyone who puts their trust in Jesus, starting with the Jews and reaching to all other peoples. We never need to feel embarrassed by the message that can rescue human souls.

The gospel shows how God makes sinners right with Himself, which is what the righteousness of God means. This right standing is received entirely by faith from start to finish, just as the prophet Habakkuk wrote that the righteous person will live by faith. Trusting in God's mercy, not our own good deeds, is the only way to have life with Him.

differ.view: Justification is God's legal declaration by which Christ's own perfect righteousness is credited to sinners through faith alone.
The righteousness of God describes God's merciful method of saving mankind through faith in Christ across both covenants rather than through the works of the law.

notes.meaning: God's holy wrath, which is His pure and settled opposition to sin, is revealed from heaven against all human godlessness and evil conduct. People show this evil by pushing down and suffocating the truth they know about God so they can keep sinning. When people fight against the truth, they put themselves under God's righteous judgment.

God holds people responsible because the essential truth about Him is plain to human reason and conscience. God Himself made this knowledge clear so that nobody could claim total ignorance. He has placed within every human being the ability to know that their Maker exists.

Ever since the world was made, God's invisible attributes, especially His endless power and divine nature, have been clearly visible in the things He created. By looking at the order and beauty of creation, the human mind can understand that an almighty Creator exists. Because of this, no one has any excuse for ignoring God or turning to idols.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Catholic Church teaches that God, the origin and end of all things, can be known with certainty from created reality by the natural light of human reason.

notes.meaning: Even though early humans had a basic knowledge of God, they refused to honor Him as God or thank Him for His daily blessings. Instead, their thinking drifted into empty and foolish ideas, and their spiritual understanding went dark. When people turn their backs on the light of God, their minds become confused and blind.

While human thinkers boasted that they were wise, their actions showed they had become complete fools. They traded away the majesty of the immortal God to worship carved statues of dying humans, birds, four-footed animals, and reptiles. Putting any created thing in the place of God turns true wisdom into absolute ruin.

Because people chose to worship images rather than God, He handed them over to the sinful desires of their own hearts. He allowed them to slide into sexual impurity and degrade their own bodies with each other. When people reject God's authority, their moral lives quickly break down.

differ.view: God's handing over of sinners is an active, judicial act where He sovereignly gives them up to the power of their lusts and the devil as punishment.
God gives sinners up by withdrawing His restraining grace, leaving them to the natural consequences of their own corrupt choices.

notes.meaning: People traded God's true nature for the lie of worthless idols, serving created things instead of the Creator Himself. Paul stops to praise God as the One who is blessed forever, reminding his readers who truly deserves all honor. Worship belongs only to the Lord who made all things, never to the things He made.

Because of their refusal to honor Him, God gave people over to shameful passions that go against His design for human sexuality. Women gave up natural relations with men for unnatural ones, and men likewise burned with lust for other men, committing shameful acts. In doing this, they experienced within themselves the painful harm and moral damage that comes from turning away from God.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern interpreters argue Paul was only condemning exploitative customs like pederasty, or heterosexual people acting against their nature, rather than committed same-sex partnerships.

notes.meaning: Since people saw no value in keeping God in their minds, He gave them up to a corrupt, undiscerning way of thinking. With their moral compass broken, they began doing things that should never be done. When the human mind rejects God, it loses its ability to tell right from wrong.

Paul provides a long list of the vices that tear human communities apart when God's restraining hand is removed. These sins include malice, greed, murder, envy, deceit, slander, hatred of God, arrogance, inventing new evils, and disobeying parents. People also became senseless, breaking promises, lacking natural family love, and showing no mercy.

Even though people know deep in their consciences that God decrees death as the just penalty for such evil, they keep doing these things anyway. Worse still, they applaud and cheer on others who do the very same wrongs. Encouraging others to sin reveals the deepest and most hardened rebellion against God.
